Rashi on Sotah 12a:10:1.hebrew: גדול הדור היה - והיו הכל נשמעין לדבריו:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:10:1.english: He was the greatest [man] of the generation - And everyone would listen to his words.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:11:1.hebrew: על הזכרים ועל הנקיבות - שלא יולידו לא זכר ולא נקיבה:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:11:1.english: Upon the males and upon the females - That they should give birth to neither a male nor a female.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:11:2.hebrew: אלא בעולם הזה - שנולדים ומתים וחוזרים וחיים הן. לעוה"ב אתה גזרת, בעולם הזה ובעולם הבא, שכיון שאינם נולדים אינן באין לעולם הבא:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:11:2.english: But only in this world - For they are born, die, and live again [at the resurrection]. You, however, decreed regarding the World to Come, [that is,] in this world and in the World to Come, for since they are not born, they do not come to the World to Come.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:14:1.hebrew: בת מאה ושלשים - כדמפרש ואזיל: שנולדה בירידתן למצרים, וישראל עמדו שם ר"י שנה. ומשנולד משה לא נתעכבו אלא פ' שנים, כדכתיב "ומשה בן שמונים שנה וגו' בדברם אל פרעה" (שמות ז), ואותה שנה יצאו. נמצא שעברו מירידתם עד שנולד משה ק"ל שנה. וכשהחזיר עמרם את יוכבד, היתה מעוברת ממשה, כדאמרינן לקמן בשמעתין:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:14:1.english: A hundred and thirty years old - As [the Gemara] explains as it goes on: that she was born at the time of their descent to Egypt, and the Israelites remained there two hundred and ten years. And from the time Moses was born they were delayed only eighty years, as it is written, "And Moses was eighty years old, etc., when they spoke to Pharaoh" (Exodus 7), and in that year they left. It turns out that from their descent until Moses was born, one hundred and thirty years passed. And when Amram took Yocheved back, she was pregnant with Moses, as we say later in this passage.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:14:2.english: For Rabbi Chama said - In [the chapter] "Yesh Nochalin" [in Bava Batra].

Rashi on Sotah 12a:14:3.hebrew: זו יוכבד - בפרטן של יורדי מצרים אתה מוצא שבעים חסר אחת, ובכללן אתה אומר "הבאה מצרימה" שבעים. זו יוכבד, שהשלימה מנינן בכניסתן לעיר:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:14:3.english: This is Yocheved - When you count the individuals among those who descended to Egypt, you find seventy minus one; yet in their total you say, "who came to Egypt, seventy." This [extra one] is Yocheved, who completed their number upon their entry into the city.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:15:1.hebrew: סימני נערות - חזרה לימי עלומיה: באורח כנשים, ובתואר פנים, ופשטו הקמטים:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:15:1.english: Signs of girlhood - She returned to the days of her youth: [she had] the menstrual cycle [lit. the way of women], and [her] facial beauty, and the wrinkles smoothed out.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:16:1.hebrew: והיא הות מיעברא ביה תלתא ירחי מעיקרא - מקמי דאהדרה, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:16:1.english: But she was pregnant with him [for] three months originally - Before he [Amram] took her back, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:16:2.english: It compares her birth, etc. This pregnancy was not written - except to expound it in this way.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:16:3.hebrew: בפיתקה של חוה - בגזר דין שלה, ושטר גזירות קללתה — דעצבון והריון:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:16:3.english: In the note of Eve - In her verdict, and the document of the decrees of her curse — of pain and pregnancy.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:17:1.hebrew: הגון לנביאות - ראתה ברוח הקודש שעתיד [להיות הגון] לנבואה:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:17:1.english: Fit for prophecy - She saw through divine inspiration that he was destined [to be fit] for prophecy.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:18:1.hebrew: ותצפנהו שלשה ירחים - שלשה חדשים יכלה להצפינו, שלא הלכו המצרים לבדוק אחריה אלא לסוף תשעה חדשים משהחזירה. והיא הוה מיעברא ביה תלתא ירחי מעיקרא, ומהכא נפקא לן:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:18:1.english: And she hid him for three months - She was able to hide him for three months, for the Egyptians did not go to search after her until the end of nine months from when [Amram] took her back. And she had been pregnant with him for three months from the beginning, and from here we derive this.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:19:1.hebrew: אמאי תצפניה ותיזיל - מאחר שצפון במסתרים היה, כדכתיב "ותצפנהו", מה יש לה לדאג:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:19:1.english: Why [could] she not hide him and go? - Since he was hidden in concealed places, as it is written, "And she hid him," what did she have to worry about?

Rashi on Sotah 12a:19:2.hebrew: ומעוי התם - וצועק שם, ודרך תינוק לצעוק כששומע קול תינוק חבירו:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:19:2.english: And he cries out there - And he shouts there, since it is the way of a baby to cry out when he hears the voice of another baby.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:19:3.hebrew: אחזו לנו שועלים - בת קול אומר למי הים: אחזו לנו שועלים הקטנים, המחבלים את הכרמים בהיותם סמדר, בעוד הפרי קטן:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:19:3.english: Catch for us the foxes - A heavenly voice says to the waters of the sea: "Catch for us the little foxes that destroy the vineyards while they are in the blossom stage, when the fruit is still small."

Rashi on Sotah 12a:1:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי דכתיב - קרא אחרינא, כי משתעי בכלב, לא קריה "בן קנז", כדכתיב בעתניאל, אלא "הקניזי" — מאנשי ביתו ומגידוליו של קנז:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:1:1.english: It is also precise, as it is written - Another verse: when it speaks of Caleb, it does not call him "son of Kenaz," as it is written regarding Othniel, but rather "the Kenizzite" — [meaning] one of the members of Kenaz's household and of those he raised.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:20:1.hebrew: שחביב עליהן ממונן - שדמיו מועטין, ואף על פי שהיה משתמר גופו יותר בשל עצים, שקשים וחזקים:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:20:1.english: That their money is dear to them - For its cost is small, even though its body [i.e., the child's body] would be better protected in [a basket] of wood, which is hard and strong.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:21:1.hebrew: דבר רך - בזה הוא משתמר יפה מן הכל, לפי שהדבר הקשה, כשהמים מוליכין אותו בחזקה, הוא נתקל והוא נישוף ונשבר; אבל דבר קל — נתקל ונזדקר באבן לאחוריו:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:21:1.english: A soft thing - In this [material the basket] is well protected from everything, because a hard object, when the water carries it along forcefully, strikes [an obstacle], gets battered, and breaks; but a light thing strikes and is thrust back off the stone [and so does not break].

Rashi on Sotah 12a:2:1.hebrew: עזובה שהכל עזבוה - שמתחילה חולנית היתה, כדקרי לה הכא יריעות, ולקמן קרי לה נמי חלאה, ועזובה — שעזבוה כל בחורי ישראל מלישא אותה:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:2:1.english: "Azuvah" [means] that everyone abandoned her - For from the beginning she was sickly, as [Scripture] calls her here "Yeriot," and below it also calls her "Chelah," and "Azuvah" — because all the bachelors of Israel abandoned her and did not marry her.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:2:2.hebrew: והא מיסב נסבה - כדכתיב "ותמת עזובה ויקח לו" וגו', אלמא איתתיה הואי:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:2:2.english: But he did marry her - As it is written, "And Azuvah died, and Caleb took for himself [Efrat]" etc.; evidently, she was his wife.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:2:3.hebrew: לשם שמים - כגון זו שהיתה חולה ונשאה לשם שמים, שבדק באחיה אהרן ומשה וראה אותם צדיקים, ורוב בנים דומין לאחי האם, בב"ב ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קי.):
Rashi on Sotah 12a:2:3.english: For the sake of Heaven - For example, this one [Miriam], who was sick, and [Caleb] married her for the sake of Heaven, because he examined her brothers, Aaron and Moses, and saw that they were righteous; and most sons resemble their mother's brothers, [as stated] in Bava Batra, in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 110a).

Rashi on Sotah 12a:3:1.hebrew: ליריעות - בלי תואר אדמומית, דמחמת חוליה היתה ירקרקת:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:3:1.english: Like curtains - Without the appearance of redness, for because of her illness she was greenish.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:4:1.hebrew: בוניה - אלו שמות בעלה שבנאה ועשאה מבונה כשאר נשים בנישואין, ובנים: ישר ושובב וארדון:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:4:1.english: Her builders - These are the names of her husband, who built her and made her "built" like other women, through marriage; and [her] sons: Yesher, Shovav, and Ardon.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:4:2.hebrew: שיישר את עצמו - מלטעות את טעות המרגלים:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:4:2.english: That he set himself straight - So as not to err the error of the spies.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:4:3.hebrew: ששיבב את עצמו - מעצתן. לשון "הבת השובבה": יוצאנית ומורדת. והכי נמי קרי ליה "מרד" בקרא אחרינא, על שם שמרד בעצת מרגלים:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:4:3.english: That he drew himself away - From their counsel. [The word *shovav* is] an expression like "the backsliding daughter" (Jeremiah 31:21): one who goes out [of bounds] and rebels. And so too he is called "Mered" in another verse, because he rebelled against the counsel of the spies.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:4:4.hebrew: שרדה ביצרו - שהיה מסיתו לטעות עמהן:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:4:4.english: He ruled over his inclination - For [his inclination] was inciting him to err along with them.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:5:1.hebrew: שהושחרו פניו - שקבל עליו תעניות הרבה, שינצל מעצת מרגלים:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:5:1.english: That his face turned dark - For he took upon himself many fasts, so that he would be saved from the counsel of the spies.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:5:2.hebrew: שנעשה לה כאב להתעסק בה ברפואות ומזונות - הצריכין לחולה:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:5:2.english: That he became like a father to her, to occupy himself with her [care] with medicines and foods - that a sick person needs.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:5:3.hebrew: שתקע את לבו לאביו שבשמים - שלא להיות בעצת מרגלים:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:5:3.english: That he fixed his heart on his Father in heaven - So as not to take part in the counsel of the spies.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:6:2.hebrew: ולבסוף נערה - שנתרפאה מחליה, וחזרה בתואר פנים כנערה:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:6:2.english: And at the end, a young woman - For she was healed of her illness and returned to a [youthful] appearance of face, like a young woman.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:7:1.hebrew: ובני חלאה - ובנייני חלאה, שנבנית ונתרפאת, משובחין היו להיות צרת וצהר ואתנן:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:7:1.english: And the sons of Helah - And the "buildings" of Helah, who was built up and healed, were praiseworthy, to be [called] Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:7:2.english: A rival to her companions - They were jealous of her beauty.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:7:3.hebrew: מוליך אתנן לאשתו - שהיה מתאוה למשכב נשים:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:7:3.english: Bringing a gift [etnan] to his wife - For he would desire sexual relations with women.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:8:1.hebrew: אף על עמו גזר - דרש רבי תנחומא: יום שנולד משה אמרו איצטגניניו: היום נולד מושיען של ישראל, ואין אנו יודעים אם מצרי הוא או יהודי. ועמד וקיבץ כל עמו, ובקש מהן ליתן לו הנולדים בו ביום, וגזר אף על עמו:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:8:1.english: He decreed even upon his own people - Rabbi Tanchuma expounded: On the day Moses was born, Pharaoh's astrologers said, "Today the savior of Israel was born, but we do not know whether he is an Egyptian or a Jew." So [Pharaoh] arose and gathered all his people, and asked them to give him those born on that day, and thus he decreed even upon his own people.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:8:2.english: At first... "and you shall put him to death" - He did not post guards, but relied on the midwives.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:8:3.english: You shall cast him - For [Pharaoh] stationed guards and *kasdorin* [officers] for this matter.

Rashi on Sotah 12a:8:4.hebrew: ולבסוף על עמו - כדפרישית. וכיון שעבר היום, ועדיין רואין איצטגניניו שלא לקה, העמיד הגזירה עד יום שהושלך ליאור:
Rashi on Sotah 12a:8:4.english: And finally, upon his own people - As I explained. And once the day had passed, and his astrologers still saw that [the savior of Israel] had not been struck, he suspended the decree until the day that [Moses] was cast into the Nile.

Tosafot on Sotah 12a:17:1.english: "Others say: he was born circumcised" - And they raise a difficulty: since Rabbi Meir said "his name was Tov," it follows that "Others" is not Rabbi Meir. But at the end of Horayot (13b) it says that they identified "Others" with Rabbi Meir, and in the first chapter of Berakhot (9b), in the Gemara on "From when does one recite the Shema in the morning?", Rabbi Meir and "Others" disagreed. And the Rabbi says that he saw in the Kuntres of France that the traditions [Rabbi Meir] received from Elisha ben Avuya were fixed in the name of "Others," because [Elisha's] name was "other" (Acher), but his other traditions were fixed in his own name. But this is not reasonable, for in the case of Rabbi Natan they identified [him with] "Some say." And do you have [any basis to say] that all of his traditions were fixed this way? And for Rabbi Meir too they did the same. Rather, it appears that after they identified him as "Others," he retracted and said, "He was born circumcised." And so too in the first chapter of Berakhot:

Tosafot on Sotah 12a:22:1.hebrew: חמר מבחוץ וזפת מבפנים - פירש רבי בשם ר"ש בר קלונימוס: זה וזה בתוך התיבה, והחמר היה מכסה את הזפת. אבל מבחוץ לא זיפפה, שלא ירגישו, כי הגומא דומה לקנה היאור, ולא יבחינו התיבה בתוך קנה היאור:
Tosafot on Sotah 12a:22:1.english: Clay on the outside and pitch on the inside - Rabbi explained in the name of R. Shimon bar Kalonymus: Both this and that were inside the ark, and the clay covered the pitch. But on the outside she did not coat it with pitch, so that they would not notice [it], for the reed [used for the ark] resembles the reeds of the Nile, and they would not distinguish the ark among the reeds of the Nile:
